transcript.answer: Lore's web UI uses one WebSocket per browser tab, served by lore-api at `/api/ws` (ADR-048, PR #2122, 2026-09-23). It replaced the earlier Server-Sent Events stream for the run page from ADR-037. The socket carries JSON text frames with client-chosen channel ids, so it multiplexes named channels. A `run` channel forwards an assembly run's pod events and transcript to everyone registered for that run. It uses a token minted by POST /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream-token. A `plan` channel tunnels the plan editor's Hocuspocus collaboration bytes to the same collaboration server. The collab-token handshake stays inside the tunnel. The web-ui holds the socket in a provider above every page, so navigating from a plan to its run keeps the connection. On the server side, there is one feed per run, fed by Postgres NOTIFY fan-out. The frame contract and cursor semantics are unchanged from the SSE design. The browser connects directly to lore-api via LORE_WS_URL (wss://<lore-api host>/api/ws). The old SSE route, the web-ui SSE proxy and the EventSource hook were removed.
